bib.title: SEED-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs with Generative Comprehension

question: How can generative comprehension of multimodal LLMs be evaluated objectively and at scale across image and video?
hypothesis: A larger multiple-choice benchmark with human-verified answers and likelihood-based scoring gives a more stable, objective comparison than small or GPT/human-judged benchmarks.
contributions: 19K human-verified multiple-choice questions over 12 spatial and temporal dimensions
A question-generation pipeline with automatic filtering and manual verification
Evaluation of 18 models and a planned leaderboard

method.summary: Questions are generated by ChatGPT/GPT-4 from foundation-model captions, detections and OCR for CC3M images, and from ground-truth annotations for videos. Questions answerable by three text-only LLMs are dropped and humans verify the rest. Models are scored by option log-likelihood.

datasets.name: SEED-Bench
datasets.size: 19K questions (19242 per Table 1); 85 (text recognition) to 4649 (instance localization) per dimension
datasets.source: derived from CC3M, SSV2, Epic-Kitchen 100, Breakfast
datasets.preprocessing: CC3M images kept only if Tag2Text caption has more than 5 nouns; 5.52% of questions removed by text-only LLM filter; humans discard unanswerable, no-correct or multi-correct questions

datasets.name: CC3M (spatial source)
datasets.preprocessing: captions regenerated with Tag2Text; images with no more than 5 nouns dropped

datasets.name: Breakfast
datasets.source: fine-grained action segmentation annotations, used for procedure understanding

models.name: ChatGPT
models.architecture: question generator for all dimensions except reasoning, and distractor generator for video

models.name: GPT-4
models.architecture: question generator for the visual reasoning dimension

models.name: Vicuna-7B, Flan-T5-XXL, LLaMA-7B
models.architecture: text-only filters; questions all three answer correctly are removed

other.note: filter uses Flan-T5-XXL, evaluation table lists Flan-T5-XL

models.name: 18 evaluated models (3 LLMs: Flan-T5-XL, Vicuna-7B, LLaMA-7B; 12 ImageLLMs; 3 VideoLLMs VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, Valley-13B)

other.imagellms: BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, InstructBLIP Vicuna, LLaVA, MiniGPT-4, VPGTrans, MultiModal-GPT, Otter, OpenFlamingo, LLaMA-Adapter V2, GVT, mPLUG-Owl
other.pandagpt: named in the Sec 4.1 list but has no row in Table 3 or Fig 1

models.name: Visual information extractors: BLIP-2, Tag2Text, SAM, VinVL attribute detector, GRiT, PaddleOCR

inference.decoding: answer ranking: compute likelihood of each option's content given the question, pick the highest
inference.samples: not stated; one pass per question, no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: question plus option text scored; no A/B/C/D letter output required; per-model prompt templates and frame counts for video not stated

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: proportion of correctly answered multiple-choice questions relative to the total number of questions; Spatial = mean of 9 dims, Temporal = mean of 3 dims, Overall = averaged across all 12 dimensions

baselines: text-only LLMs (Flan-T5, Vicuna, LLaMA) as no-vision baseline
other benchmarks MME, LAMM, LVLM-eHub, MMBench in Table 1
eval.protocol: Single run, no variance or significance reported. Ground truth from human annotation, no human/GPT judge during evaluation.

prompts.purpose: question generation, shared default instruction (full text and per-dimension instructions in Fig 4)
prompts.text: You are an AI visual assistant that can analyze a single image. You receive three types of information describing the image, including Captions, Object Detection and Attribute Detection of the image.

results.claim: On procedure understanding the best model VPGTrans is only about 5% above LLaMA.
results.quote: only 5% higher than that of LLaMA

results.claim: InstructBLIP series gain under 2% over LLMs on Something-Something-v2 action recognition (out-of-distribution).
results.note: Paper says lower than 2%; Fig 5 panel order in the extracted text is ambiguous so this was not cross-checked.

results.claim: Top model InstructBLIP reaches only about 40% on spatial relations.
results.quote: only achieves 40% accuracy on the evaluation of spatial relations

results.claim: Apart from InstructBLIP all models score below 40% on text recognition.
InstructBLIP is top on 8 of 12 dimensions; authors attribute it to 16M instruction-tuning samples and a frozen LLM (conjecture, not ablated).
results.quote: InstructBLIP achieves top performance on 8 of 12 evaluation dimensions
results.note: Explanations (a) 16M samples, (b) frozen LLM are untested hypotheses.

limits: Question and distractor generation depends on ChatGPT/GPT-4 over captions and detections from other models, so errors and style bias of those models can enter; humans only verify.
Likelihood ranking depends on option text length and phrasing and is not how chat models are used.
Five of seven spatial-dimension bar charts are given as leaderboards only; no variance, seeds or confidence intervals; single run.
Dimension sizes are very uneven (85 to 4649); authors plan to balance them.
Video input handling (frame count, sampling) per model is not stated.
Image sources are CC3M web captions, so there may be overlap with pretraining data of evaluated models; contamination is not discussed.
Authors say they use ground-truth video annotations because automatic temporal extraction is unreliable.
Models from July 2023 only; later models have far surpassed 53%.
